questions.q: An actor asks the playwright: "What does she want from him in this scene?" Which concept is the actor using?
questions.explain: A task (zadacha, Hapgood's "objective") is what the character is actively trying to do to a partner here and now.

questions.q: Why do some translators prefer "task" over "objective"?
choices: The Russian zadacha suggests a problem or job to be done, not a fixed target
questions.explain: Hapgood's "objective" fixed the American term; Benedetti's "task" is closer to the Russian.

questions.q: A character's tasks in every scene serve one deep aim across the play. What is that aim called?
questions.explain: The super-objective is the deepest want, which the through-line of action strings the tasks toward.

choices: The facts of the play the actor must accept: who, where, when, what has happened
questions.explain: Stanislavski borrowed the phrase from Pushkin; the playwright supplies them.

questions.q: A playwright writes: "I'm sad because you left me." Thinking like Stanislavski, what's the problem?
choices: It states the feeling instead of giving the actor a playable task, leaving nothing underneath to play
It breaks the unity of time
questions.explain: Playable tasks are active verbs aimed at a partner; stating the subtext flattens it.

questions.q: What is the popular story that American "beats" came from Russian-accented "bits"?
questions.explain: It's widely repeated but not established.

questions.q: Which later emphasis did Stanislavski move toward in his last years?
choices: Physical actions: truthful actions in the given circumstances, with feeling following
questions.explain: The so-called method of physical actions; Strasberg's American Method leaned more on the earlier emotion-memory work.

ideas: An actor should ask not "who am I?" but "what would I do if I were in this situation?"
Divide a role into bits, each with a task: an active verb aimed at a partner.
All of a character's smaller tasks serve one deepest aim, strung together by a through-line of action.
Find a sequence of truthful physical actions and feeling will follow.
